text:
For almost 54 minutes nobody scored, and it looked like Carolina would win the way Carolina wins. Then Nikolaj Ehlers snapped one in at 13:41 of the third, set up by Logan Stankoven, who won a puck battle to keep it in the zone, and the Hurricanes' win chance jumped to 87%. They had won four in a row. A fifth looked close.

Lane Hutson had other plans. Eighty seconds after Ehlers scored, the Montreal defenseman tied it at 15:01, from Nick Suzuki and Cole Caufield. Then, 38 seconds into overtime, he did it again, Suzuki feeding him for the winner. Hutson played 27 minutes and 36 seconds, scored both Montreal goals and added 0.88 wins by our count, the most of anyone on the ice. Not bad for a player who went 62nd overall in 2022.

The game itself was dead even. Carolina had 70 shot attempts to Montreal's 46, but the Canadiens blocked 22 shots and the chance quality landed at 3.18 expected goals for Montreal and 3.15 for Carolina (expected goals measure how good the chances were, not just how many). Our replays of every shot split it 50-50. On nights like that, goalies decide it.

Both were excellent. Jakub Dobes made 26 saves on 27 shots and saved 2.15 goals more than those shots deserved, including what Cory Lavalette of the North State Journal called a game-saving stop on Ehlers. Pyotr Kochetkov stopped 22 of 24, saved 1.18 above expected, and made the biggest save of the night on Phillip Danault in overtime, moments before Hutson ended it.

Montreal needed this one. Chris Kreider is out six to eight weeks with a lower-body injury, per NHL.com, and the Canadiens have been leaning on young players all month, from Jacob Fowler's Calder push to Dobes in this start. They head home on a two-game winning streak. Carolina, which won October's meeting 6-4, loses a streak but not much else: more of the puck, one goal against in regulation, and a night when the other goalie was a little better.
headline: Lane Hutson scores twice to steal one in Raleigh
